Produces three panels and nothing else:

* `supp_fig10a_combined` — read depth vs mean relative abundance, by provenance
* `supp_fig10b_combined` — per-sample gut vs non-biological / impossible-clade load
* `supp_fig10c_combined` — per-sample gut coverage against the detection thresholds

```{r knitr-opts, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse   = TRUE,
  comment    = "#>",
  message    = TRUE,   # the dropped-sample / missing-crypt notes belong in the record
  warning    = TRUE,
  dpi        = 150,
  fig.width  = 18,
  fig.height = 10,
  fig.path   = "./"   # committed alongside the .md
)
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, forcats, readr
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
```

## 1. Config

```{r config}
INPUT_FILE <- "kraken_metaphlan_consensus_species.tsv"
CRYPT_FILE <- "../Data/Main_Outputs/crypt_signature_attributions.csv"
ANNOT_FILE <- "./taxon_annotation.R"   # shared blacklist/allowlist module
OUTDIR     <- "./"

RANK            <- "s"    # "s" species, "g" genus, "t" SGB
READ_LEN        <- 150    # mean read length (bp)
PAIRED          <- TRUE   # TRUE if counts are read PAIRS
MIN_READS_TAXON <- 10     # reads needed to call a taxon "detected" in a sample
DEFAULT_GENOME  <- 4.0e6  # fallback genome size (bp)

N_TOP          <- 20      # taxa shown in the fig 10a bar panel
MAX_TAXA_SHOWN <- 5       # top bin of the fig 10c stacked bar ("5+")

# Genome sizes (bp), keyed by species name or genus, for coverage maths.
GENOME_SIZES <- c(
  `Escherichia coli` = 5.0e6, `Bacteroides fragilis` = 5.2e6,
  `Faecalibacterium prausnitzii` = 3.1e6, `Fusobacterium nucleatum` = 2.4e6,
  `Cutibacterium acnes` = 2.5e6, `Klebsiella pneumoniae` = 5.5e6,
  Escherichia = 5.0e6, Shigella = 4.6e6, Klebsiella = 5.5e6, Salmonella = 4.8e6,
  Bacteroides = 5.5e6, Parabacteroides = 6.2e6, Prevotella = 3.5e6,
  Faecalibacterium = 3.1e6, Roseburia = 3.9e6, Eubacterium = 3.5e6,
  Blautia = 6.0e6, Ruminococcus = 3.5e6, Bifidobacterium = 2.3e6,
  Lactobacillus = 2.2e6, Enterococcus = 3.0e6, Clostridium = 4.0e6,
  Akkermansia = 2.7e6, Fusobacterium = 2.4e6, Streptococcus = 2.1e6,
  Staphylococcus = 2.8e6, Pseudomonas = 6.3e6, Cutibacterium = 2.5e6,
  Ralstonia = 5.5e6, Bradyrhizobium = 8.5e6, Sphingomonas = 4.0e6,
  Stutzerimonas = 4.7e6, Natronomonas = 2.8e6, Arthrobacter = 4.5e6,
  Elizabethkingia = 4.1e6, Paenibacillus = 6.0e6
)

stopifnot(file.exists(INPUT_FILE), file.exists(CRYPT_FILE), file.exists(ANNOT_FILE))
source(ANNOT_FILE)                      # annotate_taxa(), score_evidence()
dir.create(OUTDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## 2. Load and build the count matrix

MetaPhlAn/Bracken lineage tables are nested — a phylum row already contains its
genera — so exactly one rank is selected rather than all rows.

```{r load}
raw <- read.delim(INPUT_FILE, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE,
                  comment.char = "#", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(raw)[1] <- "clade_name"

# restrict to the crypt samples; this also drops non-sample columns such as
# NCBI_tax_id, so no numeric-coercion filtering is needed afterwards
crypt_samples <- unique(read.csv(CRYPT_FILE)$sample)
missing_cols  <- setdiff(crypt_samples, names(raw))
if (length(missing_cols))
  warning(length(missing_cols), " crypt sample(s) absent from the profile table: ",
          paste(head(missing_cols, 5), collapse = ", "))

raw <- raw[, c("clade_name", intersect(crypt_samples, names(raw))), drop = FALSE]
raw[-1] <- lapply(raw[-1], as.numeric)

last_tok  <- sub(".*\\|", "", raw$clade_name)
rank_code <- sub("__.*", "", last_tok)
taxon     <- sub("^[a-z]__", "", last_tok)

keep <- rank_code == RANK
if (!any(keep))
  stop("No rows at rank '", RANK, "'. Present: ",
       paste(unique(rank_code), collapse = ", "))

mat <- as.matrix(raw[keep, -1, drop = FALSE])
rownames(mat)  <- taxon[keep]
lineage        <- raw$clade_name[keep]
mat[is.na(mat)] <- 0
mat <- round(mat)

nz      <- rowSums(mat) > 0
mat     <- mat[nz, , drop = FALSE]
lineage <- lineage[nz]

empty <- colSums(mat) == 0
if (any(empty)) {
  message("Dropping ", sum(empty), " sample(s) with 0 classified reads.")
  mat <- mat[, !empty, drop = FALSE]
}

samples <- colnames(mat)
libsize <- colSums(mat)
relab   <- sweep(mat, 2, pmax(libsize, 1), "/")

cat(sprintf("Loaded %d taxa at rank '%s' across %d samples.\n",
            nrow(mat), RANK, length(samples)))

ann <- annotate_taxa(rownames(mat),
                     rank = if (RANK %in% c("s", "t")) "s" else "g",
                     gut_catalogue = NULL, lineage = lineage)
stopifnot(identical(ann$taxon, rownames(mat)))
```

## 3. Thresholds and genome-equivalent coverage

Three per-taxon, per-sample thresholds. They are never comparable to a sample's
total read count summed over taxa.

* **`T_DETECT`** — presence/absence only. A few reads says "seen", nothing more.
* **`T_BREADTH`** — coverage at which a call can be *verified* by checking that
  reads spread across the genome rather than piling onto conserved or repetitive
  regions. Below it, a real low-abundance organism and a misassignment artefact
  look identical.
* **`T_QUANT`** — reads needed to *compare* abundance between samples. Counts
  carry Poisson shot noise, so `SE(log ratio) = sqrt(1/k1 + 1/k2)` and resolving
  a fold-change `F` at power `1-beta` needs
  `k >= 2 * ((z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta}) / log(F))^2`. This is a floor: it
  assumes pure Poisson sampling, whereas real microbiome counts are
  overdispersed. A taxon below `T_QUANT` cannot support an abundance comparison
  at *any* sample size, because the limit is per-sample shot noise, not n.

`T_USABLE` requires both: breadth (to believe the call) and shot-noise headroom
(to resolve the effect). Breadth is by far the more demanding of the two.

```{r thresholds}
bases_per_read <- READ_LEN * (if (PAIRED) 2 else 1)
cov_of <- function(reads) reads * bases_per_read / DEFAULT_GENOME

reads_for_fold <- function(fold, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) + qnorm(power)
  ceiling(2 * (z / log(fold))^2)
}

T_DETECT        <- MIN_READS_TAXON
T_BREADTH_X     <- 0.05                                           # coverage, in X
T_BREADTH_READS <- ceiling(T_BREADTH_X * DEFAULT_GENOME / bases_per_read)
T_QUANT_2X      <- reads_for_fold(2.0)
T_COVERAGE     <- max(T_BREADTH_READS, T_QUANT_2X)

# taxa x samples, in X
gsize <- unname(GENOME_SIZES[ann$name])
alt   <- unname(GENOME_SIZES[ann$genus])
gsize[is.na(gsize)] <- alt[is.na(gsize)]
gsize[is.na(gsize)] <- DEFAULT_GENOME
cov_mat <- sweep(mat * bases_per_read, 1, gsize, "/")

c(detect = T_DETECT, quant_2x = T_QUANT_2X,
  breadth = T_BREADTH_READS, coverage = T_COVERAGE)
```

## 4. Provenance labels

One label per taxon, shared by all three figures so the colour scale matches.
Levels are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, so they sum to the library size and
can be stacked directly.

`impossible_clade` is split out from `contaminant` deliberately. Both are
non-biological, but a blacklist call can be argued with on grounds of list
curation, whereas a halophilic archaeon in a colonic crypt cannot.

```{r provenance}
PROV_LEVELS <- c("contaminant", "impossible_clade", "gut", "oral",
                 "unclassified", "unnamed_sgb")

prov <- rep("unclassified", nrow(mat))
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "unnamed_sgb"]   <- "unnamed_sgb"
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "oral"]          <- "oral"
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "gut"]           <- "gut"
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "environmental"] <- "contaminant"
prov[ann$blacklist_status == "contaminant"]   <- "contaminant"
prov[ann$env_clade]                           <- "impossible_clade"  # overrides
prov <- factor(prov, levels = PROV_LEVELS)

PROV_COL <- c(contaminant  = "firebrick",   impossible_clade = "grey60",
              gut          = "darkslateblue", oral           = "goldenrod",
              unclassified = "grey60",      unnamed_sgb      = "grey80")

PROV_LAB <- c(contaminant  = "Contaminant", impossible_clade = "Impossible clade",
              gut          = "Gut bacteria", oral            = "Oral bacteria",
              unclassified = "Unclassified", unnamed_sgb     = "Unnamed SGB")
```

## 5. Figure data

```{r figure-data}
## --- 10a: one row per taxon ---------------------------------------------
contam <- score_evidence(
  ann, mat, blanks = NULL,
  read_len = READ_LEN, paired = PAIRED, genome_sizes = GENOME_SIZES,
  min_reads = MIN_READS_TAXON, default_genome = DEFAULT_GENOME
)
i <- match(contam$taxon, rownames(mat))
stopifnot(!anyNA(i))
contam$total_reads <- rowSums(mat)[i]
contam$mean_relab  <- rowMeans(relab)[i]
contam$provenance  <- prov[i]

## --- 10b: one row per sample, composition by provenance ------------------
fig2 <- data.frame(sample = samples, total_reads = as.integer(libsize),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (p in PROV_LEVELS)
  fig2[[paste0("relab_", p)]] <-
    colSums(mat[prov == p, , drop = FALSE]) / pmax(libsize, 1)

# combined non-biological load: blacklisted contaminants PLUS impossible clades
fig2$relab_nonbiological <- fig2$relab_contaminant + fig2$relab_impossible_clade

## --- 10c: one row per sample, gut coverage vs thresholds -----------------
gmat <- mat[prov == "gut", , drop = FALSE]
gcov <- cov_mat[prov == "gut", , drop = FALSE]

fig3 <- data.frame(
  sample    = samples,
  gut_reads = as.integer(colSums(gmat)),
  # the honest per-organism number: summing coverage across taxa overstates
  # what can be done with any single one of them
  max_gut_coverage_X = apply(gcov, 2, max),
  # counts of INDIVIDUAL gut taxa clearing each per-taxon bar in this sample
  n_gut_detected        = colSums(gmat >= T_DETECT),
  n_gut_coverage       = colSums(gmat >= T_USABLE_2X),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r theme}
fig_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.title   = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
        axis.text    = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"))
```

## 6. Supplementary Figure 10a

```{r fig10a}
fig10a_scatter <- ggplot(contam, aes(total_reads, mean_relab, colour = provenance)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PROV_COL, labels = PROV_LAB, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Total reads across samples",
       y = "Mean relative abundance across samples",
       colour = "Species classification") +
  fig_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

fig10a_bar <- contam %>%
  slice_max(mean_relab, n = N_TOP) %>%
  ggplot(aes(mean_relab, fct_reorder(species, mean_relab), fill = provenance)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PROV_COL, labels = PROV_LAB, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "Mean relative abundance\nacross samples", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  fig_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

supp_fig10a_combined <- fig10a_scatter + fig10a_bar + plot_layout(widths = c(3, 1))

ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, "supp_fig10a_mean_read_abundance_all_bacteria.png"),
       supp_fig10a_combined, width = 18, height = 10, dpi = 200)

supp_fig10a_combined
```

```{r}
  filter(provenance%in%c('impossible_clade','contaminant'))%>%

print(paste0('Percent contaminant ',pct_contam))
```

```{r}
  filter(provenance%in%c('gut'))%>%

print(paste0('Percent gut taxa ',pct_gut))
```

## 7. Supplementary Figure 10b

A high *minimum* contaminant fraction across samples means this is a property of
the protocol (low input, 10–12 PCR cycles), not of a few outlier libraries. The
impossible-clade panel is the unarguable version of the same point: those reads
have a true abundance of zero in every sample.

```{r fig10b}
pct_nonbio_over_half <- round(100 * mean(fig2$relab_nonbiological > 0.5))

fig10b_contaminant <- ggplot(fig2, aes(relab_gut, relab_nonbiological)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linewidth = 1, linetype = 5, colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 0.5, hjust = 1.02, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 6, colour = "black",
           label = sprintf("Contaminant taxa > 50%% of reads\n[%d%% of samples]",
                           pct_nonbio_over_half)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Combined relative abundance of gut taxa per sample",
       y = "Combined relative abundance of contaminant taxa per sample") +
  fig_theme

fig10b_impossible <- ggplot(fig2, aes(relab_gut, relab_impossible_clade)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Combined relative abundance of gut taxa per sample",
       y = "Combined relative abundance of 'impossible taxa' per sample") +
  fig_theme

supp_fig10b_combined <- fig10b_contaminant | fig10b_impossible

ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, "supp_fig10b_relab_nonbio_impossible.png"),
       supp_fig10b_combined, width = 18, height = 10, dpi = 200)

supp_fig10b_combined
```

```{r}
fig2%>%
  summarise(median=round(median(relab_nonbiological),2),
            lower_q=round(quantile(relab_nonbiological,0.25),2),
            upper_q=round(quantile(relab_nonbiological,0.75),2)
            )
```
```{r}
fig2%>%
  summarise(median=round(median(relab_impossible_clade),2),
            lower_q=round(quantile(relab_impossible_clade,0.25),2),
            upper_q=round(quantile(relab_impossible_clade,0.75),2)
            )
```

## 8. Supplementary Figure 10c

```{r fig10c}
taxa_counts <- fig3 %>%
  select(detected     = n_gut_detected,
         coverage = n_gut_coverage) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "threshold", values_to = "n_taxa") %>%
  mutate(threshold = factor(threshold,
                            levels = c("detected", "coverage")),
         n_taxa = case_when(
           n_taxa == 0  ~ "0",
           n_taxa <= 5  ~ "5",
           n_taxa <= 10  ~ "10",
           n_taxa <= 20 ~ "20",
           n_taxa <= 50 ~ "50",
           n_taxa > 50  ~ "50+"
         ),
         n_taxa = factor(n_taxa,
                         levels = c("0", "5", "10","20", "50", "50+"))) %>%
  count(threshold, n_taxa, .drop = FALSE)

fig10c_detectable <- ggplot(taxa_counts, aes(n_taxa,n, fill = n_taxa)) +
  geom_bar(stat='identity',position='dodge',colour = "black") +
  facet_grid(~threshold,
             labeller=labeller(threshold=c('detected' = "Nominal read based detection\n[mapped reads > 10 ]",
                              'coverage' = "Genome coverage based detection\n[mapped coverage > 0.05X]"))) +
            
               
  
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = c('0','5','10','20','50','50+'),
    labels = c(`0` = "0",`5` = "0-5", `10` = "5-10", `20` = "10-20",
               `50` = "20-50",`50+` = "50+")) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`50+` = "grey0",  `50` = "grey25", `20` = "grey40",
               `10` = "grey60", `5` = "grey75", `0` = "grey90"),
    labels = c(`0` = "0",`5` = "0-5", `10` = "5-10", `20` = "10-20",
               `50` = "20-50",`50+` = "50+")) +
  labs(x = "Number of gut taxa identified in crypt", y = "Number of crypts", 
       fill = NULL) +
  fig_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text   = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
        strip.background=element_blank()
        )

ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, "supp_fig10c_gut_taxa_coverage.png"),
       fig10c_detectable, width = 16, height = 8, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
  summarise(median=median(n_gut_coverage),
            lower_qr=quantile(n_gut_coverage,0.25),
            upper_qr=quantile(n_gut_coverage,0.25),
            max=max(n_gut_coverage))
```
